subject: INLA crashes when using over 43k rows

messages.author: 10d91be380c625bc
messages.subject: INLA crashes when using over 43k rows
parts:
Hej! 


I am experimenting with INLA, and my dataset has 73k rows. 
In order to run `inla(...)` without it crashing, I must reduce down to 43k rows.

Is this on purpose? Am I misunderstanding something?

Here's some added information, just in case:


inla_stats_model <- inla(
  formula = death ~ X + Y,
  data = simulated_dataset %>% 
    slice(1:43e3),
  family = "binomial",
  verbose = TRUE,   silent = FALSE
)

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA crashes when using over 43k rows
parts:
I guess you're running on Windows, as it seems it has some problems
running larger models. can you try on a Mac or a Linux machine?

also the model

death ~ X + Y

would be relative slow, compared to the simple solution

glm(death ~ X + Y)

INLA does include the linear predictor into the latent field, but with
only fixed effects, then its not a good strategy....

Best
H

Thanks much.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA crashes when using over 43k rows
parts:
the 'glm' comment, was only that

> x = rnorm(10)
> y = rnorm(10)
> r = glm(y ~ 1 + x, data = data.frame(y,x))

for large n, not 10 as here, essentially gives to Bayes solution,

so

> coefficients(r)
(Intercept) x
-0.2850354050 0.1549605004
> vcov(r)
(Intercept) x
(Intercept) 0.06541832349 -0.03019982099
x -0.03019982099 0.05452811315



gives the posterior mean and covariance, essentially.

this is, due to how the model is coded internally in INLA, must faster
than a inla() call, especially for large n and few covariates.

H
